hint: WASD to walk  ·  E to talk  ·  the north gate for the Tower, the south gate for the road

spots.line: A fat ginger cat asleep in the reeds by the pond, a duck feather stuck to his chin. He lets you carry him, complaining all the way.
The shrine of the unnamed: a cairn of offering-stones and three candle stubs. You light them. One goes out. When you look again, it is burning.
Chalk on the alley wall: a crown with a line struck through it, and under it a date three days off. You copy it down and leave it be.
The avenue runs straight from the gate to the Cathedral, and the Cathedral looks straight at the Tower. Everyone here walks it twice a day.
The Margrave's banners hang over the lane, a crown on blue. Somebody has climbed up and turned one of them inside out.
Washing strung between two houses, a shirt for every size of person and three for a size nobody is.
Cabbages and beans in rows by the south wall. Every inch inside the walls is worth growing something on.
The south gate stands open. The queue to come in through it does not move.
Caravans camp here the night before, so they are first through in the morning. They are never first.

chests.line: A strongbox wedged behind a rain barrel, and the barrel was the only lock.
A loose cobble by the wall, with somebody's savings under it.
A sack dropped in the alley. Whoever ran from the Watch dropped it.
A crate fallen off a cart, and nobody has come back for it.

props.line: A fountain with a stone king in it, holding a stone sword up at the Tower. Pigeons have opinions about him.
North: the Cathedral. West: Market Row. East: Tavern Lane and the Gilded Flagon. South: out.
One arm points north, up the high street: THE TOWER. The other points out of the gate: EVERYWHERE ELSE.

buildings.name: the Margrave's hall
shut: Two of the Watch cross their spears in front of you. Not today. Not you.
The Margrave is not receiving. The Margrave is never receiving.

buildings.name: the counting house
shut: Ledgers to the ceiling and a clerk who does not look up.

buildings.name: the clock hall
shut: The clock inside is three minutes slow. It has been three minutes slow for a hundred years, and the city sets itself by it.

buildings.name: a merchant's house
shut: Shutters closed. Somebody inside is counting out loud.

buildings.name: the dyer's house
shut: The dyer's hands are blue to the elbow. She waves you off with one.

buildings.name: a lodging house
shut: No rooms. Try the Flagon.

buildings.name: the Adventurers' Guild hall
shut: The city's Guild hall: a long room of maps and arguments. Wenna at its door keeps the contracts.

buildings.name: the scrivener's
shut: Fennick does his writing out front, where the light is.

buildings.name: a tall house
shut: Somebody upstairs is learning the fiddle. Nobody downstairs is enjoying it.

buildings.name: a carter's cottage
shut: Out on the road. Back in a week, or never, the neighbour says.

buildings.name: the burnt chandlery
shut: Burnt out last winter. Candles, it turns out, burn.

buildings.name: the cooper's
shut: Hammering. The cooper doesn't stop to answer.

buildings.name: the moneylender's
shut: A grille, a ledger and a smile. You back away.

buildings.name: a narrow house
shut: Nobody in. A board nailed across the door says the house is the Margrave's, and the Steward will hear offers.
Empty since the winter. Through the shutters: a hearth, a bed frame, and a lot of dust waiting for somebody.

buildings.name: the Watch house
shut: The Watch house: cells at the back, Captain Edda out front.

buildings.name: Ada's bakery
shut: Warm in there. Ada does her selling outside.

buildings.name: the butcher's
shut: Hooks, cleavers and a dog with ambitions.

buildings.name: the chandler's
shut: Candles, rope and lamp-oil, all shut up for the day.

buildings.name: the stables
shut: Horses, and the smell of horses.

buildings.name: Gunnar's brewhouse
shut: Vats and steam. Gunnar does his talking out front.

buildings.name: a weaver's house
shut: Looms clacking. Nobody comes to the door.

buildings.name: a quiet house
shut: A woman answers, looks at you, and shuts it again.

buildings.name: a baker's widow's
shut: She's at the market. She's always at the market.

buildings.name: the tailor's
shut: Pins in his mouth. He waves.

buildings.name: a crowded house
shut: Nine children answer the door at once.

buildings.name: a sailmaker's
shut: Canvas everywhere, and no sea for forty miles.

buildings.name: a fence's house
shut: Whoever answers says nobody lives here, and shuts the door on you.

buildings.name: a house with blue shutters
shut: The shutters are blue. The door is shut.

buildings.name: the toll house
shut: The toll house is shut. The tollmaster collects outside, where he can see you coming.

buildings.name: the waystation
shut: Full. A caravan from the south has every bed and most of the floor.

people.name: Ada the Baker
chatter: Hot bread! Hot-ish bread!
Puddi-ing! Pudding! ...Has anyone seen a cat?

hello: Bread? Rolls? You've not seen a ginger cat? Fat, looks offended? He's mine.
Morning! It's always morning in a bakery. That's the trouble.
talk.again: Back for more? Good. Everybody comes back. It's the yeast.

ask.q: How big is this city?
ask.a: Walk it end to end and your bread's gone cold. Walk it round the walls and it's gone stale.

talk.shop: Bread this morning, bread this afternoon. Pies at noon, if the oven's in a mood.

job.ask: You said something about a cat?
job.offer: Pudding. Ginger, fat, answers to nothing. He goes out every night and comes back every morning, and this morning he didn't. He likes water. He likes ducks more.
job.thanks: Bless you. Try the park. Try anywhere with ducks.
job.hand_over: He was asleep in the reeds by the pond. He's home.
job.done: PUDDING. You great orange idiot. ...Thank you. Here, and take a loaf, and don't argue.

people.name: Brother Oswin
chatter: The Cathedral faces the Tower. So does every grave in our yard.
Dawn rite at dawn. Dusk rite at dusk. We are not imaginative.

hello: Peace on your road. Have you come for the rite? You've missed it. Everyone misses it.
A traveller. You have the look of somebody walking towards the Tower.

ask.q: Why does the Cathedral face the Tower?
ask.a: So we remember. Everyone who climbed it, everyone who didn't come down. The city was built by people who stopped climbing.

ask.q: Does everyone want to climb the Tower?
ask.a: No. Most of the people in this city came here instead of climbing. Some came here instead of dying. I don't ask them which.

job.ask: Is there anything I can do?
job.offer: The shrine of the unnamed, in the yard behind the Cathedral. Three candles, one for each who climbed this year and didn't come back. My knees won't take the yard. Would you light them?
job.thanks: Behind the Cathedral, on the east side. You'll see the stones.
job.done: Thank you. I'll say their names at dusk. If you'd like a name said, tell me, and I'll say that too.

talk.bye: Go carefully. The Tower is patient.

people.name: Gunnar the Brewer
chatter: Best ale in the city. Ask anybody. Ask Marta. Don't ask Marta.
Barley's up. Everything's up.

talk.hello: Gunnar. Brewer. Don't touch the vats.

ask.q: Marta at the Flagon sent me for her barrel.
ask.a: About time she sent someone with arms. There. Roll it, don't carry it, and if it's dented it's yours.

ask.q: Who drinks the most in this city?
ask.a: The Watch. Then the priests. Then everybody else, all at once, on market day.

talk.shop: Ale. If you wanted anything else, you've come to the wrong door.

people.name: Captain Edda of the Watch
chatter: The Watch sees everything. The Watch just doesn't always say.
Don't loiter by the Margrave's door. He hates a crowd.

hello: Captain Edda. The Watch. If you've done something, now's the time to say so.
You again. Stay out of trouble or stay where I can see you.

ask.q: Is the city safe?
ask.a: Safer than out there. That's a low wall to step over, mind.

ask.q: What does the Watch do?
ask.a: Shuts the gate at dark, opens it at dawn, and in between stops ten thousand people killing each other. Mostly the stopping.

job.ask: Anything the Watch needs a hand with?
job.offer: Somebody's been chalking marks on walls round Tavern Lane. A crown with a line through it. Could be children. Could be a date. Find me one and copy it down. Don't rub it off.
job.thanks: Try the alley off Tavern Lane. They like the alleys.
job.hand_over: Here: a crown, struck through, and a date three days off.
job.done: Three days. Right. You've done the city a service, and the city will forget it by morning. I won't.

talk.bye: Go on. And keep out of the alleys after dark.

people.name: Fennick the Scrivener
chatter: Letters written, read, answered, and lost. Prices on the board.
My hand cramps in the cold. Write faster, then.

talk.hello: Fennick. I write what people can't and read what they won't.

ask.q: What do people write here?
ask.a: Wills, mostly. Everyone walking towards the Tower wants to leave something behind first. You'd be surprised how many leave it to their dog.

job.offer: A letter for Steward Hobb, at the Margrave's hall. The Watch won't let me near the door since the business with the goat. They'll let you.
job.thanks: Into Hobb's hand, not the guard's. The guard eats paper.
job.done: Good. Then I get paid, and so do you.

talk.bye: Don't sign anything you can't read.

people.name: Steward Hobb
chatter: The Margrave is not receiving.
Appointments are made in writing. Writing is made at Fennick's.

talk.hello: The Margrave is not receiving. I am the Steward. I am also not receiving.

ask.q: A letter for you, from Fennick the scrivener.
ask.a: Fennick. Hm. ...It's about the goat. It's always about the goat. Tell him I've read it. Tell him nothing else.

ask.q: Who is the Margrave?
ask.a: The Margrave holds the city for the crown, and the crown has not been seen in forty years. Draw what conclusions you like, quietly.

ask.q: The narrow house on the east street. Is it for sale?
ask.a: To people who live in the city, yes. You sleep in a ditch, by the look of you. Take a room somewhere and keep it, and come back when you are a resident.

ask.q: We keep a room at the Flagon now. The narrow house (2 gold 25 silver)?
ask.a: Two gold and twenty-five silver. Sign here. And here. The key. The roof is sound, the chimney draws, and the last tenant is not coming back for anything, so don't ask. It's yours: your bed, your strongbox, your door. The Margrave thanks you for your residence, through me.

ask.q: About our house.
ask.a: Your house is on the books and the books are in order. That is all I ever wish to say about any house.

people.name: Sergeant Brask
chatter: Keep left. Keep moving. Keep your hands where I can see them.

rounds.line: Watches the gate a while.
Stands in the crossroads, looking important.
Salutes the Cathedral, out of habit.
Moves a beggar off the Cathedral steps.

people.name: Watchman Pol
chatter: West wall, east wall, Tavern Lane, back. Twenty years. My boots know it without me.

rounds.line: Turns at the west wall.
Turns at the east wall.
Looks in at the Tavern Lane end.
Peers through the Flagon's window.

people.name: Lugg the Porter
chatter: Barrel up, barrel down. My back's older than I am.

rounds.line: Shoulders a barrel from the brewhouse.
Heaves it in at the Flagon's door.
Fetches a sack of oats from the stables.
Drops a load of iron at the smithy.

people.name: Marigold the Fishwife
chatter: Herring! Eels! Something I can't name but it's fresh!

rounds.line: Cries the herring.
Sells eels along Market Row.
Swaps a fish for a cabbage at the stall.

people.name: Old Tallow the Lamplighter
chatter: Every lamp in the city, every night. I've never seen the city dark. I'd like to, once.

rounds.line: Trims the lamp.
Lights the lamp by the apothecary.
Lights the crossroads lamp.
Lights the lamp on the corner.

people.name: Nell the Sweeper
chatter: Horse muck, cabbage leaves, and a tooth this morning. Somebody's tooth.

rounds.line: Sweeps the gate square.
Sweeps the crossroads.
Sweeps outside the Guild hall, and is ignored.

people.name: Bastian the Merchant
chatter: Everything has a price. Most things have two.

rounds.line: Haggles at a stall on Market Row.
Buys a bolt of cloth, then sells it back.
Counts his coin by the fountain.

people.name: Saffi of the Spices
chatter: Saffron! Pepper! Something red that makes you cry!

rounds.line: Arranges the spice jars.
Trades a pinch of pepper for a roll.
Sells cinnamon to the fishwife.

people.name: Widow Amsel
chatter: My husband climbed the Tower. I come and sit where I can see it.

rounds.line: Sits on the bench, facing the Tower.
Feeds the ducks in the park.
Lights a candle at the old shrine.

people.name: Lark the Busker
chatter: ♪ Oh the Tower is tall and the Tower is grey ♪
♪ ...and nobody came back down that way ♪
Coin for the song? Coin to stop?

talk.hello: A song? Only a copper. Two to stop.

ask.q: Sing something.
ask.a: ♪ One climbed for gold and one climbed for fame, and one climbed because the others came. And one sat down at the foot of the stair, and said, I'll stay. Somebody should be there. ♪

ask.q: Who was the one who sat down?
ask.a: Nobody knows. That's why it's a good song.

talk.bye: Mind how you go. If you don't come back, I'll put you in a verse.

people.name: a boy running errands
chatter: Can't stop! Message for the Watch!
Can't stop! Message from the Watch!

people.name: a reveller who missed his bed
chatter: The Flagon closed? No, I closed. The Flagon's still open.
Which way's... which way?

people.name: a sellsword between contracts
chatter: Guild's got nothing but rats and letters. I didn't learn the sword to stick rats.
Heard there's a gate breaking in the east. Heard it twice.

people.name: a cat on the wall
chatter: The fox in the hat regards you. It is not a cat. Nobody here has noticed.

people.name: a gate guard
chatter: Gate shuts at dark.
Move along.

people.name: a gate guard
chatter: Nothing gets in after dark. Nothing has tried in a while. That's what worries me.

people.name: Muck Muck
chatter: That wall's leaning. Everyone says it's fine. It isn't fine.
Measure twice. Then once more, because you weren't listening.

hello: Muck Muck. Builder. If it's standing in this city, odds are I put it there, or I'm the one they called when it fell down.
Mind the rubble. That's the bathhouse, or it will be again.
talk.again: Back again? Something needs building, then. It always does.

ask.q: Everyone says to ask you. Why?
ask.a: Because I'm still here. Forty years of roofs, wells, walls and one bridge I don't talk about. When something needs building in Stormreach, they come and find Muck Muck.

ask.q: What happened to the bathhouse?
ask.a: Somebody let the boiler run dry. I've told the Margrave I'll have it back up by spring. I've told him that for three springs.

ask.q: Could you build something for us?
ask.a: Bring me ground of your own and coin to match, and I'll put a roof on it that outlasts you. Until then, I've got a bathhouse.

ask.q: Could you build something for us?
ask.a: You've shut a gate, so the Guild will vouch for you, and you've ground of your own: that crater you came down in. Flattest ground for a mile, and you cleared it for free. Nobody will fight you for it. Pay me and I'll start: a smithy, an infirmary, then a wall, and people will come.

ask.q: Build a smithy at the crater (75 silver).
ask.a: A forge, an anvil and a roof over both, and a smith to work them: I know one who's sick of the city. It'll be standing when you next walk in.

ask.q: Build an infirmary at the crater (75 silver).
ask.a: Cots, clean water and a healer who isn't Sinner. Sinner taught her, mind. It'll be up when you're back.

ask.q: Put a wall round the crater (1 gold 25 silver).
ask.a: Timber, all the way round, with a gate on the south side. Folk go where there's a wall. You'll have neighbours by the time you see it.

ask.q: How's our crater?
ask.a: Better than my bathhouse. Go and look at it.

talk.bye: Off you go. Watch the scaffold.

people.name: Sinner
chatter: Bring them in. Whatever they did, I've done worse.
A cut left alone is a grave dug slowly.

hello: Sinner. Yes, that's what they call me, and yes, I've earned it. I mend people now. For a price.
Somebody's bleeding on my step. Is it one of yours? Come in.
talk.again: Back so soon? Who's hurt this time?

ask.q: Why do they call you Sinner?
ask.a: Because I was one, loudly, for a long time. Then I learned to close wounds instead of opening them. The name stayed. I kept it so I don't forget.

ask.q: Are you a priest of the Cathedral?
ask.a: The Cathedral and I have an arrangement. They don't come down here, and I don't go up there.

heal.done: There. Whole again, every one of them. Try to stay that way.
heal.whole: Nobody here needs me. Come back when somebody does.

talk.bye: Out you go. I'd rather not see you again soon.

people.name: Wenna the Guild Clerk
chatter: Contracts for the city are posted inside. Contracts for everywhere else, out here with me.
Every company comes through this gate in the end. I keep the list, and I cross them off it.

people.name: Tollmaster Crane
chatter: Name, business, and a copper for the gate.
No goats past the gate. No exceptions. Two exceptions.

hello: Name, business, and a copper for the gate. The copper is the important part.
Through you go. Mind the queue. Mind the goats.

ask.q: What's in there?
ask.a: Everything. A cathedral, a market, the Watch, the Gilded Flagon. Ten thousand people who all think they're the only one in a hurry.

ask.q: Who rules the city?
ask.a: The Margrave, on paper. The Watch, on the street. The brewers, after dark.

ask.q: Why the walls?
ask.a: Because of the gates out there. When one breaks, the whole country runs for the nearest wall. We'd sooner they ran to us than over us.

talk.bye: Keep your purse in front of you, and your hand on it.

people.name: a pilgrim come for the dawn rite
chatter: Three days walking to hear one rite. I'll be late for it, I know I will.
They say the Cathedral was built facing the Tower. I want to see it before my eyes go.

people.name: Hask the Caravan Guard
chatter: Forty days from the dunes and the gate shuts on us at dusk.
Ask me about wolves. No, don't.

rounds.line: Warms his hands at the cold fire, out of habit.
Counts the barrels again.
Waters the mules at the trough.

people.name: Peg the Goat-seller
chatter: Goats! Fine goats! Not allowed in the city, so cheap!

talk.hello: Goats! Fine goats! Not allowed in the city, which is why they're cheap.

ask.q: Why aren't goats allowed in?
ask.a: One ate the Margrave's hat. Not this Margrave, his father. Grudges in there outlive the people.

talk.shop: No goats for you, then. Cheese? It's goat.
talk.bye: Tell them in there Peg sent you. They won't care, but tell them.

people.name: Ensign Rowe of the Watch
chatter: Off the road, please. Carts coming.
Gate's open, walls are up. Nothing to report. I'd quite like something to report.

rounds.line: Looks out down the road.
Walks the inside of the wall.
Checks the far corner.
Has a word with whoever's at the gate.
